page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.64-512 is a high-capacity, general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz. It provisions 64 dedicated physical cores configured with simultaneous multithreading to deliver 128 dedicated vCPUs. System memory is sized at 512 GB, matching the platform standard of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU (8 GB per physical core). This core-to-memory balance positions the server for applications that require extensive parallelism and consistent memory allocation per thread.

The hardware configuration contains no local storage drives and includes no hardware acceleration GPUs. Persistent storage operations and operating system files must be deployed via external block storage volumes, which decouples compute scaling from disk capacity. For ingress and egress networking, the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address to enable direct Internet routing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high x86 thread density and proportional RAM capacity without the added expense of specialized accelerator hardware or high-tier memory-optimized ratios. The absence of local solid-state drives avoids paying for unneeded ephemeral storage, though it introduces a requirement for networked storage management. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.64-512 is technically suited for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, large-scale web application deployments, batch data processing, and container orchestration clusters that need dedicated compute execution.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.64-512 is a large-format general-purpose virtual machine designed for high-concurrency enterprise workloads. Driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7742 processor running at 2.25 GHz, the instance delivers 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated virtual CPUs with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 512 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. The server profile contains no integrated GPU accelerators and offers no bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on external block storage services for persistent data. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned for network connectivity. By offering broad thread density and proportional memory capacity without the overhead of physical accelerator hardware, the instance provides cost-effective throughput for horizontally scalable architectures. VM.Standard.E3.Flex.64-512 is well aligned with heavy enterprise web serving, backend services, batch data processing, distributed compilation, and general-purpose microservice clusters.
